text:
In Pittsburgh, the talk is about who goes, not who plays. The Penguins have 16 points from 19 games, our playoff model gives them a 19% chance, and the trade chatter has climbed all the way up the roster: Pierre LeBrun reporting the Hurricanes' interest in Erik Karlsson (per NHLTradeRumor.com), Minnesota outlets asking whether the Wild should chase Evgeni Malkin, and TribLIVE's Mark Madden asking "Is the unthinkable now thinkable for Sidney Crosby and the Penguins?" For now Malkin is skating beside Crosby and Rickard Rakell, the spot Bryan Rust (on injured reserve until about Dec 5) held before he went down.

The Senators bring a story of their own. Nick Cousins is out after Jakob Chychrun's hit in the Capitals game, a check the league reviewed and let stand; TSN reported Travis Green saying Cousins was knocked unconscious and will miss 7 to 10 days. Ottawa answered by beating Colorado 4-3 in overtime after trailing in the third, Shane Pinto scoring the winner on his birthday. They're 3-1-1 in their last five with 54% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), and our model has them at 77% to make the playoffs. Philip Tomasino, back in Pittsburgh for the first time since leaving (59 games as a Penguin), is one point from 100.

Linus Ullmark, our projected starter for Ottawa, has been the best story in the Senators' season so far: .938 and 8.2 goals saved above expected, a year after he finished 13.3 below. For Pittsburgh we have Sergei Murashov in over Arturs Silovs (12 of 19 starts) after his shootout win in San Jose; he's at -0.5 this season.

Our sleeper is Fabian Zetterlund, a third-liner at about 14:32 a night who has played beside Tim Stützle and Dylan Cozens since William Eklund went on injured reserve. He has 3.2 expected goals in his last 10 games, better than 93% of depth forwards, and Pittsburgh gives up the 10th-most expected goals per 60. We have him at 18% to score and 36% for a point.
headline: Trade talk swirls as the Senators visit Pittsburgh
